messages:
maya: Quick thread — saw a weird divergence after int8 PTQ on the new reranker. NDCG@10 basically flat but pairwise ordering consistency between short vs long queries dropped a lot. Anyone seen this pattern before?

oscar: Hmm can you paste the aggregate numbers? short/long pairwise consistency sounds specific. :thinking:

maya: Sure, ran a quick batch: 
```
baseline (fp16): pairwise_consistency_short_long = 0.818
int8-ptq: pairwise_consistency_short_long = 0.731
ndcg@10 delta = -0.003 (not sig)
mrr delta = -0.012 (p~0.04)
```
Not huge NDCG movement but ordering flips for many pairs where short query had higher context priming.

linh: Did you keep the same priming examples across short and long? sample/priming bias can cause that — model may be relying more on primed context after quant.

maya: Yep same prompt templates. Priming set mostly short-context examples (we were optimizing for latency earlier), so that could bias.

anika: Could be sample selection + quant noise. If the positive contexts are short, quantization might amplify preference for local signals. Worth trying length-balanced priming and candidate sampling.

ravi: Also try pairwise_consistency metric with bootstrapped CIs. NDCG can hide ordering instability. Bootstrapped 95% CI might show the significance of the consistency drop.

eval-bot: Batch eval summary uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/7712345678/pairwise_run.json
Command: ```./run_rerank_eval --model rerank-v2-int8 --cohort short,long --metrics ndcg@10,mrr,pairwise_consistency --seed 42 --save s3://redwood-evals/7712345678```

oscar: Can you run a quick controlled test: same candidate pool, two priming variants (short-primed vs balanced-primed) and report pairwise_consistency broken down by query length buckets?

maya: Ran a 2k-sample probe this morning, quick numbers: 
```
short-primed (int8): pairwise_consistency = 0.72
balanced-primed (int8): pairwise_consistency = 0.79
baseline (fp16, balanced): 0.82
```
So balancing priming recovers a lot of the consistency. NDCG differences still tiny.

linh: Nice. That points to priming distribution mismatch. Also want to check anchor doc length — if ranking head uses absolute position features, quant noise could change subtle score ties.

anika: Suggest we add deterministic sampling and a fixed candidate ordering seed to ensure flip counts are stable. Also compute pairwise_flip_rate per decile of doc length.

maya: Agree. Next steps I propose:
- run 10k balanced-priming probe across same candidate pool (seeded)
- compute pairwise_consistency and flip_rate by query_len_bucket and doc_len_bucket
- bootstrap CIs (n=1000)
- compare kv-cache-on vs kv-cache-off (we've seen kv packing interact with int8 in past)

ravi: I'll set up the job on dedicated GPU pool, using --deterministic-sampling and attach which model artifact used. Add a small sanity check that score ties are stable (hash scores mod 1e-6).

oscar: Can we also try a tiny calibration layer (single bias) post-quant to see if flips reduce? Might be cheaper than redoing priming.

maya: Good idea — I'll run bias-calib on top of int8 and report pairwise_consistency delta.

linh: One more ask: include candidate text normalization (strip html, unicode norm) in both runs. We had small tokenizer drift before.

maya: Will include. TL;DR: likely priming/sample bias amplified by int8 -> run balanced priming + bootstraps + kv-cache toggles + small calibration. Will post results here. :eyes:
